sampling_model.design: Independent uniform complete randomization on \(B\) and \(S\), with exactly \(n_B\) treated buyers and \(n_S\) treated sellers.
sampling_model.units: The finite populations \(B\) and \(S\) and all dyad potential outcomes are fixed; assignment is the only randomness.
sampling_model.treatment: A dyad has exposure \((z_i^B,z_j^S)\in\{0,1\}^2\); the tested contrast compares \((1,1)\) with \((0,0)\).
sampling_model.overlap: No superpopulation overlap condition is used; positivity is the finite support condition \(h(a,b)\ge R\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None. The procedure enumerates or exactly samples the conditional randomization law.

body.tldr: For independently and uniformly half-randomized populations on two unequal market sides, the optimal covering rectangle at a required support \(R\) is reduced to a finite residual catalog depending only on \(R\). For \(R\ge 4\) and \(n_B,n_S\ge 4R\), the exact frontier is the maximum of finitely many affine catalog scores, and the phase inequalities retain every catalog tie. A constant-incidence sampler implements the selected event, and null-adjusted focal outcomes yield exact one-sided inversion for a sharp constant total effect. No universal collapse of the catalog to diagonal unit residuals is claimed.

project_justification.gap: The closest exact two-sided-market method proves validity for selected equal blocks and treats block choice heuristically; general biclique methods establish validity and power guidance but do not classify the optimal covering paired rectangle. Existing one-dimensional subset-sum purification does not preserve a prescribed common buyer--seller target fiber.
project_justification.niche: Balanced independent randomization converts admissible covering rectangles into two coupled half-sum profiles. This structure permits an exact finite residual reduction and affine phase analysis while retaining unequal market-side sizes, without asserting an unrestricted-biclique optimum.
project_justification.fill: A two-stage concentration argument bounds the residual on the smaller side and uses a support-preserving residual-copy comparison to bound the larger residual. This yields a finite catalog, an exact affine frontier with all catalog ties, an implementable conditional law, and exact one-sided sharp-null inversion. Whether every catalog entry can be purified to a dominating diagonal unit-residual entry remains a separate open question.

body.related_work: Liu, Shaikh, and Toulis (2026) establish the equal \(k\)-block total-effect test and motivate the support--focal-size trade-off; the present result optimizes over covering paired rectangles through a finite residual catalog. Puelz, Basse, Feller, and Toulis (2022) encode imputable tests as bicliques and motivate large bicliques, but do not supply the paired-rectangle classification. Basse, Feller, and Toulis (2019) provide the conditioning-mechanism validity theorem used after imputability is verified. Basse, Ding, Feller, and Toulis (2024) provide the orbit-equivariance template, while unequal rectangular profiles require a separate constant-incidence count. Luo, Dasgupta, Xie, and Liu (2021) provide discrete Fisher inversion machinery, specialized here after null-adjusted dyadic imputability and crossing monotonicity are established. Singhal (2019) motivates bilinear subset-sum profiles and one-dimensional purification, but does not furnish a coupled common-fiber-preserving reduction to diagonal unit residuals. Ye et al. (2023) provide the unequal-side marketplace consumer through Platform O's independent user-view and ad randomizations.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The conditioning event must be selected without outcomes. Raw focal outcomes are not imputable under a nonzero sharp constant effect, so the null-adjusted array \(Q_\tau\) is essential. Complement symmetry implies that an ordinary nonrandomized absolute-score test has minimum \(p\)-value at least \(2/h(a,b)\), so support \(20\) cannot support an ordinary two-sided test at level \(0.05\). In addition, the finite catalog has not been proved to collapse universally to the diagonal unit-residual subcatalog: known one-dimensional purification arguments do not preserve the required joint buyer--seller target fiber.
body.honest_scope: The note proves the finite residual catalog, exact affine frontier and catalog equality cases, constant-incidence sampler, and exact one-sided inversion under the sharp constant total-effect null. Universal unit-residual purification remains an explicit unresolved question and is not used by those results. The note makes no claim about weak-null validity, power or confidence-width optimality, unrestricted bicliques, minimality of the \(4R\) threshold, ordinary two-sided \(95\)-percent inversion at support \(20\), or the empirical validity of the constant-effect exposure model for Platform O.
body.interpretation: The finite-catalog result is the actionable design certificate: for fixed resolution \(R\), one enumerates \(\mathcal C_R\), evaluates the affine scores at the observed pair of market sizes, and retains every maximizer on a phase boundary. The unresolved unit-residual question concerns only whether this already finite computation admits a further universal closed-form collapse; it is not needed for catalog optimality, sampling, or exact one-sided inversion.
